hasEvidenceItems.description: The variant H93R is shown to be loss-of-function through both in vivo neuronal morphology assays and in vitro biochemical PIP3 dephosphorylation assays. While the protein stability is normal, the catalytic activity and ability to rescue the knockout phenotype are significantly impaired.

value.message: This paper (PMID:29373119) self-reports multiple experimental systems: in vivo rescue assay (soma size/morphology) (functionally_abnormal); biochemical lipid phosphatase activity (functionally_abnormal); protein stability assay (functionally_normal). It is recommended to go back to the relevant part of the full text and manually confirm which of these is genuinely the most direct functional evidence for the overall direction below (there is a past instance of an indirect results table being cited by mistake).

This judgment (PMID:29373119) is based on a single study only. For criterion codes on the ClinGen side that require reproducibility across multiple studies (e.g., PS3_Moderate or stronger), this evidence alone may not be sufficient in strength.
No approved-assay list is registered for PTEN VCEP, so institutional applicability could not be checked automatically for any of this paper's (PMID:29373119) experiments.

The experiments in this paper (PMID:29373119) disagree on direction (in vivo rescue assay (soma size/morphology) = functionally_abnormal; biochemical lipid phosphatase activity = functionally_abnormal; protein stability assay = functionally_normal), yet the LLM confidently concluded PS3. This conflict was detected automatically and the judgment has been forced to not_clear (real-world instance: PTEN c.112C>T, where VAMP-seq showed functionally_normal but the Akt-activation assay showed functionally_abnormal, and the LLM adopted only the latter).

value.label: in vivo rescue assay (soma size/morphology): functionally_abnormal
value.detail: mouse (dentate gyrus neurons), readout: neuronal soma size and pS6 signaling, vs GFP-PTEN (wild-type) and Pten KO - H93R was unable to rescue the neuronal hypertrophy or increased pS6 signaling caused by Pten KO.; H93R expressed in wild-type mice induced a significant increase in soma size (dominant negative effect).

value.label: biochemical lipid phosphatase activity: functionally_abnormal
value.detail: HEK293 cells, readout: PIP3 levels via ELISA, vs Wild-type PTEN and Pten KO - Expression of the H93R mutant was unable to restore PIP3 levels to control levels in Pten-deficient HEK293 cells.

value.label: protein stability assay: functionally_normal
value.detail: HEK293 cells, readout: protein half-life (cycloheximide chase), vs GFP-PTEN (wild-type) - The H93R mutation displayed no change in stability compared to control.

These results demonstrate a clear functional abnormality in protein-membrane interaction compared to wild-type PTEN.

hasEvidenceItems.description: The paper identifies p.His93Arg as an active site variant that is enzymatically inactive but maintains wild-type-like protein abundance. Because the assay measures abundance rather than enzymatic activity, it provides evidence that the variant does not affect stability, but it cannot be used as PS3 evidence for loss of function, nor BS3 for normal function in the context of its catalytic role.
